yaml.description: What the user actually sees: the web platform itself, the JavaScript ecosystem on top of it, and the Python shortcuts for when you do not want any of that.
yaml.title: Front End

markdown.markdown:
<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

There are two routes to a user interface here, and the site covers both without pretending one is correct.

The first is the real one: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, then a framework, a bundler, a linter, and a build step. The second is to skip it, and let a Python library generate the interface. That is the right answer more often than front-end developers like to admit, particularly for a dashboard or a model demo, which is most of what gets built in this collection.

Nearly every page assumes a Django REST Framework backend, because that is what these interfaces are put in front of. See [Back End](https://bthek1.github.io/Back_End/) for that half.

---


Python libraries that generate the interface, ordered by how much control they give up.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Streamlit](01_1_Streamlit.ipynb) | The most detailed of these. A script becomes a web app, which is why it wins for internal tools |
| [Gradio](01_2_Gradio.ipynb) | The same idea aimed at model demos, an input, an output, and a shareable link |
| [Plotly Dash](01_3_Plotly_Dash.ipynb) | Flask, Plotly.js, and React underneath, exposed as Python. More work than Streamlit, more control in return |
| [fastHTML](05_fastHTML.ipynb) | HTML generated from Python, without the JavaScript layer |
| [Grafana](03_Grafana.ipynb) | Not a framework at all. Point it at a time-series source and you have dashboards without writing an interface |

---

## The Web Platform

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [HTML](04_HTML.ipynb) | The markup itself |
| [CSS](06_CSS.ipynb) | Styling |
| [Bootstrap](07_Bootstrap.ipynb) | The CSS and JavaScript component framework that saves writing most of it |
| [SVG](18_SVGs.ipynb) | Vector graphics in the browser, at length |
| [Markdown](15_Markdown.ipynb) | The lightweight markup behind most documentation, including this site |
| [HTTP Headers](16_HTTP_Headers.ipynb) | Message headers, how Nginx sets them, and CORS, which is the one that breaks a front end against an API |

---

## JavaScript and Its Toolchain

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [JavaScript](Javascript/00_Javascript.ipynb) | Writing the front end against a DRF API |
| [Fetch API](Javascript/01_Fetch_API.ipynb) | Promise-based HTTP requests, replacing XMLHttpRequest |
| [jQuery](Javascript/02_JQuery.ipynb) | The older way, still met in existing code |
| [TypeScript](10_Typescript.ipynb) | Optional static typing over JavaScript, compiling back down to it |
| [Node](08_Node.ipynb) | JavaScript on the server, its core concepts and ecosystem |
| [npm](09_npm.ipynb) | Dependency management for all of the above |
| [Webpack](11_Webpack.ipynb) | Bundling code, styles, and assets into what the browser actually loads |
| [Prettier](13_Js_Prettier.ipynb) | Opinionated formatting across JS, TS, HTML, CSS, and JSON |
| [ESLint](14_ESLint.ipynb) | Linting, for the errors formatting cannot catch |
| [Highcharts](Javascript/03_Highcharts.ipynb) | Charting driven from a DRF endpoint |
| [DataTables](Javascript/04_Datatables.ipynb) | Sortable, searchable tables |
| [SurveyJS](19_SurveyJS.ipynb) | The JSON format for defining forms and surveys |

---

## React

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [React Overview](React/02_React_Overview.ipynb) | Fundamentals through to modern patterns and ecosystem tooling |
| [React Setup](React/03_React_Setup.ipynb) | Getting a project running |
| [React Init](React/01_React_Init.ipynb) | The initial scaffold |
| [React Libraries](React/04_React_Libraries.ipynb) | The npm add-ons worth knowing, grouped by what they do |
| [React and Django](React/05_React_%26_Django.ipynb) | The full-stack pairing: project structure, how the two halves communicate, deployment, and practice |
| [React with Docker](React/06_React_Docker.ipynb) | A production setup for Django, DRF, React, and PostgreSQL together, using multi-stage builds, Nginx for static files, and Compose to orchestrate it |

## Flutter

The mobile and desktop route, where one codebase targets Android, iOS, Linux, Windows, and macOS.

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [Flutter Setup](Flutter/01_Flutter_Setup.ipynb) | Getting the toolchain working |
| [Widgets](Flutter/02_Widgets.ipynb) | The framework's whole model is that everything is a widget |
| [Dart](Flutter/03_Dart.ipynb) | The language underneath |
| [Riverpod](Flutter/04_Riverpod.ipynb) | State management |

---

## Being Found and Measured

| Page | Covers |
|---|---|
| [SEO](SEO/01_SEO.ipynb) | Split into three layers, of which a full-stack developer owns one completely, shares one, and should refuse the third |
| [Website Metrics](17_0_Website_Metrics.ipynb) | Tracking traffic and behaviour through analytics, heatmaps, and log analysis |
| [Google Analytics](17_1_Google_Analytics.ipynb) | Wiring GA into a Django project |

---

## Not Covered Yet

- **No Vue, Svelte, or Angular.** React is the only JavaScript framework covered.
- **Nothing on accessibility**, which is the omission that matters most in a front-end reference.
- **No testing.** Neither component testing nor browser automation appears anywhere.
- **Nothing on state management in React** specifically. Riverpod covers it for Flutter, but Redux, Zustand, and the modern alternatives are absent.
- **No responsive or mobile-web design page**, despite Bootstrap being covered.
- **Four stubs at two to three cells**: [React Init](React/01_React_Init.ipynb), [Fetch API](Javascript/01_Fetch_API.ipynb), [jQuery](Javascript/02_JQuery.ipynb), and [Google Analytics](17_1_Google_Analytics.ipynb).
- Web performance, bundle size, and Core Web Vitals go unmentioned even though Webpack and metrics both have pages.

---
